description: §6.7.4 a reactive effect written inside an `<each>` row body is registered (one per row), not dropped. Its body writes no reactive cell (S447: an effect drives the outside world), so the run is observed through the DOM it touches: one row, #inc bumps @n once, the row's effect sets data-ran on #beacon. Carried on impl#1 (S432 P7; re-pinned S449 from each/when-changes-in-row-body, whose writing body S447 made an error): the block is dropped from the row render, silently.
rationale: §6.7.4 Scope and teardown: "**An `<effect>` inside an `<each>` row is one effect per row**, registered when the row is created and unregistered when the row is removed"; the keyword `when … changes { }` "IS an `<effect>`" during its §63 window. Not on mount (beacon untouched until #inc); a call to a platform API is not a reactive write (§6.7.4 rule 5).
